profile.summary: IntelliFold predicts the all-atom structure of a biomolecular complex from its sequences, in the manner of AlphaFold 3. The current release, IntelliFold-2, takes an AlphaFold 3 style JSON input listing the chains and ligands, runs a Pairformer trunk and a diffusion sampler, and writes predicted coordinates with confidence scores. The developers report it on FoldBench against AlphaFold 3, Boltz, Chai-1 and Protenix, with the gains concentrated in antibody-antigen interfaces and protein-ligand co-folding. Code and weights are Apache-2.0 and the weights are hosted on Hugging Face; a hosted server runs a further variant that is not released.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: header, Inference and License; release note: Introduction and Benchmark Performance

summary_quotes.text: We compared IntelliFold against several leading methods, including [Boltz-1,2](https://github.com/jwohlwend/boltz), [Chai-1](https://github.com/chaidiscovery/chai-lab), [Protenix](https://github.com/bytedance/Protenix) and [Alphafold3](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3).
with a focus on antibody-antigen interactions and protein-ligand co-folding.
The IntelliFold project, including code and model parameters, is made available under the [Apache 2.0 License](./LICENSE), it is free for both academic research and commercial use.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: IntelliFold follows the AlphaFold 3 design: a Pairformer trunk over token representations feeding a diffusion module that generates all-atom coordinates. The release note describes what changed in version 2. The latent representations inside the Pairformer blocks were widened, which the authors say both raises capacity and improves hardware utilisation. The atom attention mechanism was reformulated for consistency between training and inference, and atom-level tokenisation is applied stochastically. The diffusion sampler was fine tuned with Proximal Policy Optimization, treating the sampler as a stochastic policy, which the authors say reduces unstable or low-quality trajectories. Training used a focal-loss style reweighting that puts more gradient on hard examples, and the Protein Data Bank was reprocessed with an updated pipeline alongside a larger self-distillation dataset. The release note calls PPO-enhanced sampling and the difficulty-aware loss exclusive to IntelliFold-2-Pro, the server-only variant, so the released IntelliFold-2 and IntelliFold-2-Flash weights do not include them. At inference an optional steering mode adds, at every denoising step, the gradient of a set of differentiable physical potentials covering bond lengths and angles, clashes, chirality, planarity, van der Waals overlap, covalent connections and symmetric chain repulsion.

quotes.text: Latent Space Scaling: We increase the dimensionality of latent representations within the Pair- former blocks, significantly enhancing the model’s capacity to capture complex biological interac- tions.
Improved Hardware Utilization: Larger hidden dimensions increase arithmetic intensity, lead- ing to substantially higher Model FLOPs Utilisation (MFU)
We revise the atom attention mechanism to a more principled formulation, ensuring robust and self-consistent model behaviour during training and inference.
Stochastic Atomization: Atom-level tokenization is applied stochastically to improve robustness
We apply reinforcement learning, instantiated via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to fine-tune the diffusion module and improve sampling reliability at inference time.
To address imbalance in training signals across structural difficulty levels, we adopt a focal-loss–style reweighting formulation.

We re-processed the Protein Data Bank (PDB) dataset using an updated pipeline to ensure high-fidelity supervisory signals. Furthermore, we scaled up the self-distillation dataset and optimised its distribution.

add `--steering` to nudge the
diffusion sampler at every denoising step with the gradient of a set of differentiable
physical/chemical potentials (bond lengths & angles, internal clashes, chirality, double-bond / ring
planarity, protein–ligand van-der-Waals overlap, covalent connections, and symmetric-chain
repulsion)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three variants of version 2 exist, and only two are released. IntelliFold-2-Flash has 12 standard Pairformer blocks and is offered for academic use and fine tuning; IntelliFold-2 has 48 widened Pairformer blocks with latent space scaling and is the most accurate released model; IntelliFold-2-Pro adds PPO-enhanced sampling and difficulty-aware loss and runs only on the developers' server. The Hugging Face repository holds intellifold_v0.1.0.pt from the first release, intellifold_v2.pt, intellifold_v2_flash.pt, and the JAX conversion intellifold_v2.bin.zst with intellifold_v2_fourier.npz, at the revision read here. Since June 2026 the repository runs version 2 on the AlphaFold 3 JAX engine, vendored at version 3.0.3, and the JAX weights were converted from the PyTorch checkpoint with convert_ifv2_to_jax.py. A result should name the variant, the weight file, the engine and whether steering was on, because steering changes the sampler.

quotes.text: IntelliFold-2-Flash: A fast, efficient model intended primarily for academic use and easy fine- tuning, featuring our updated data curation and multiscale structural representations with 12 standard Pairformer blocks.
IntelliFold-2: Our most accurate open-source model, featuring 48 widened Pairformer blocks with latent space scaling.

IntelliFold-2-Pro: Our server-side flagship model. In addition to all architectural improvements, it incorporates exclusive PPO-enhanced sampling and Difficulty-Aware Loss optimization for max- imum precision.
IntelliFold-2-Flash and IntelliFold-2 are available at https://github.com/IntelliGen-AI/IntelliFold. IntelliFold-2-Pro is available to Pro users via our online server at https://server.intfold.com.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: All-atom biomolecular structure prediction model of the AlphaFold 3 family, with a diffusion sampler and optional physical steering.
facts.source_locator: README: title and Inference; release note: Introduction

quotes.text: # IntelliFold: A Controllable Foundation Model for General and Specialized Biomolecular Structure Prediction
This major architectural update establishes a new state-of-the-art as one of the first open-source models to outperform AlphaFold 3 [2] on Foldbench [3].

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Pairformer trunk plus diffusion module. IntelliFold-2 uses 48 widened Pairformer blocks with latent space scaling; IntelliFold-2-Flash uses 12 standard blocks. Inference runs on the AlphaFold 3 JAX engine, vendored at version 3.0.3.
facts.source_locator: release note: Introduction and Key Technical Changes; README: Acknowledgements

quotes.text: featuring 48 widened Pairformer blocks with latent space scaling
with 12 standard Pairformer blocks

This repository runs IntelliFold-v2 on the **AlphaFold 3** JAX inference engine by Google DeepMind ([Apache-2.0](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3)), vendored at [`third_party/alphafold3/`](third_party/alphafold3) (v3.0.3).

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An AlphaFold 3 style JSON file listing the chains and ligands, optionally carrying its own multiple sequence alignments and templates. Without them the AlphaFold 3 data pipeline builds alignments from downloaded sequence databases. A directory of such JSON files can be run as a batch.

quotes.text: The input is an [AlphaFold 3-style JSON](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/main/docs/input.md).

**Search MSAs yourself** — if your JSON has no MSAs, first download the sequence databases, then point
`--db_dir` at them (AF3 runs its data pipeline to build MSAs/templates)

**Batch a directory across every GPU** — predicts every JSON in the directory (one worker per GPU,
self-balancing local queue, resumable — rerun to continue)

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted all-atom structures written to the directory given by --output-dir. The developers' own evaluation reports LDDT for monomers and DockQ for interfaces, and PoseBusters validity and ligand RMSD for small molecule poses.
facts.source_locator: README: Inference; release note: Table 1 caption and Figure 1 caption

quotes.text: intellifold predict fold_input.json --model-dir=model_v2 --output-dir results -- --norun_data_pipeline
We report LDDT for monomers and % DockQ > 0.23 for interaction systems.
it raises the PoseBusters validity rate from **~72% to ~93%**

strengths.text: Inference runs on the AlphaFold 3 JAX engine, which the developers adopted because it is fast and Apache-2.0 from version 3.0.3.

quotes.text: AlphaFold 3's JAX inference is fast, and as of [**v3.0.3** it is released under the **Apache-2.0** license](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/releases/tag/v3.0.3) — so we leverage their repository to accelerate IntelliFold-2 inference.

strengths.text: The optional steering mode improves physical plausibility of ligand poses without retraining: on the developers' own PoseBusters-v2 evaluation the validity rate rises from about 72 per cent to about 93 per cent.

This

PoseBusters-v2 evaluation it raises the PoseBusters validity rate from **~72% to ~93%**

limitations.text: The most accurate variant is not released. IntelliFold-2-Pro, with the PPO-enhanced sampling and difficulty-aware loss, runs only on the developers' server, and they recommend that server for the most accurate predictions.

quotes.text: IntelliFold-2-Pro: Our server-side flagship model.
The server runs the **full, optimized, latest** IntelliFold implementation for optimal performance.

limitations.text: A GPU with working CUDA is expected: the README deals with jax[cuda12] falling back to CPU and tells the user to reorder LD_LIBRARY_PATH. No CPU-only path is described.

quotes.text:
`jax[cuda12]` ships its own CUDA libraries and uses the GPU out of the box. **If it instead falls back
to CPU** (`cuSPARSE ... not found`), a system CUDA on your `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is shadowing the bundled
ones

limitations.text: Building alignments yourself means downloading the AlphaFold 3 sequence databases first. Only the bundled example input carries its own alignments and templates.

quotes.text:
the example `fold_input.json` already contains its MSAs and templates, so skip the
data pipeline with `--norun_data_pipeline`
bash third_party/alphafold3/fetch_databases.sh /path/to/databases

limitations.text: Steering costs time: it adds gradient evaluations inside every denoising step and triggers a separate compilation per input, so the developers advise keeping it off for large batches.

quotes.text:
Expect a
> noticeably longer wall-clock per target — only enable it when you want the improved physical
> validity; for large batches keep it off unless you specifically need PoseBusters-clean poses.

run_guide.summary: Install the vendored AlphaFold 3 engine and the intellifold wrapper, then predict the example input with the IntelliFold-2 weights downloaded on the first run.
prerequisites: A GPU with CUDA 12, since the install uses jax[cuda12] and the README treats a CPU fallback as a fault to fix.
Network access to Hugging Face for the weights, or the HF_ENDPOINT variable set to a mirror.
Disk space for the AlphaFold 3 sequence databases only if you need the data pipeline to build alignments.
Apache-2.0 terms for both code and weights.

steps.title: Clone the repository at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/IntelliGen-AI/IntelliFold
cd IntelliFold
git checkout --detach bc84487aec48e0d33bff9f8ee6cff9013ea3ab00
steps.explanation: The clone and cd lines come from the README Setup block; the checkout line is added here to pin the commit that was read.

quotes.text:
git clone https://github.com/IntelliGen-AI/IntelliFold
cd IntelliFold

steps.title: Install the AlphaFold 3 engine and the wrapper
steps.shell:
pip install ./third_party/alphafold3 && build_data
pip install intellifold
steps.explanation: The README's install for an environment that does not already have alphafold3. build_data builds the CCD data from libcifpp's bundled components.cif and needs no network.

quotes.text:
pip install ./third_party/alphafold3 && build_data
pip install intellifold        # or `pip install .` from the clone

steps.title: Fetch the example input
steps.explanation: The README's quick start downloads an example JSON that already contains its alignments and templates.

quotes.text: wget https://huggingface.co/intelligenAI/intellifold/resolve/main/fold_input.json

steps.title: Predict
steps.explanation: The README's quick start command. The weights are downloaded into ./model_v2 on the first run, and --norun_data_pipeline skips alignment building because the example input already has alignments. Everything after -- is passed to AlphaFold 3.

quotes.text: intellifold predict fold_input.json --model-dir=model_v2 --output-dir results -- --norun_data_pipeline

On the first run the pre-converted IntelliFold-v2 weights are downloaded from Hugging Face into
`./model_v2` (later runs just load them).

steps.title: Optional: steer the sampler toward physically valid poses
steps.explanation: The README's steering example. It is off by default, improves ligand pose validity and is slower.

quotes.text:
intellifold predict fold_input.json --model-dir=model_v2 --output-dir results \
    -- --norun_data_pipeline --steering

outputs: Predicted structures under the results directory given to --output-dir.
The IntelliFold-2 JAX weights cached in ./model_v2 after the first run.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
An input without alignments needs the AlphaFold 3 databases fetched with third_party/alphafold3/fetch_databases.sh and --db_dir pointed at them, which is a large download.
The repository also documents an older PyTorch route in docs/installation.md, with its own cache_data layout and a YAML input; the two routes take different inputs and should not be mixed.

notes: The record's description is phrased in antibody-antigen terms, which comes from the POISK benchmark (existing source poisk-20261115-source-manuscript-v1) and not from the developers: IntelliFold is a general biomolecular structure predictor, and antibody-antigen is one category its release note emphasises. The record names IntelliFold v2; the released variants are IntelliFold-2 and IntelliFold-2-Flash, so a result should say which. The IntelliFold 2 preprint is at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.02.09.704787v1 and was not fetched, since bioRxiv is rate-limiting this address and no PMC copy exists for that DOI; the release note PDF committed in the repository was used instead, read through its text layer. The repository also carries a NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES file that were not fetched.
